levels.title: A1 • Absolute Beginner
levels.tagline: Master the essentials: greetings, numbers, daily routine, and basic sentences.

units.title: Greetings & Introductions
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself, and learn basic polite phrases.
units.grammarSummary: German differentiates formal (Sie) and informal (du). Verbs conjugate with -e, -st, -t, -en.

lessons.title: Hallo & Tschüss
lessons.subtitle: Basic greetings and farewells
lessons.grammarTip: Use 'du' with friends and 'Sie' in polite or business settings.

words.exampleEn: Goodbye and have a nice day!

quiz.prompt: How do you politely say 'Goodbye' in German?
quiz.explanation: 'Auf Wiedersehen' is the polite standard farewell.

lessons.title: Wer bist du?
lessons.subtitle: Introductions and the verb 'sein'
lessons.grammarTip: Conjugation of 'sein': ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind.

quiz.prompt: Which form of 'sein' completes: 'Wir _____ hier'?
quiz.explanation: 'Wir' conjugates with 'sind'.

units.title: Numbers & Time
units.description: Count from 1 to 100, tell time, and schedule appointments.
units.grammarSummary: German numbers 21-99 say units first, e.g. einundzwanzig (one-and-twenty).

lessons.title: Eins, zwei, drei
lessons.subtitle: Numbers 1 through 20
lessons.grammarTip: Note: eins drops the -s in compounds (einundzwanzig).

quiz.prompt: What does 'Wie spät ist es?' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Wie spät ist es?' literally means 'How late is it?' = 'What time is it?'.

units.title: Family & Relationships
units.description: Talk about parents, siblings, children, and close friends.
units.grammarSummary: Possessive pronouns: mein/meine (my), dein/deine (your). Add -e for feminine and plural nouns.

lessons.title: Meine Familie
lessons.subtitle: Immediate family members
lessons.grammarTip: der Vater (mein Vater), die Mutter (meine Mutter), das Kind (mein Kind).

words.exampleEn: My father is reading a book.

quiz.prompt: Which is correct for 'my mother'?
quiz.explanation: 'Mutter' is feminine, so use 'meine'.

units.title: Food & Drinks
units.description: Order food in restaurants, buy groceries, and express preferences.
units.grammarSummary: The Accusative case: masculine 'der' shifts to 'den' / 'einen' when an object is acted on.

lessons.title: Im Restaurant
lessons.subtitle: Ordering drinks and meals
lessons.grammarTip: 'Ich möchte...' (I would like...) takes the accusative case.

words.exampleEn: We would like to pay, please!

quiz.prompt: Complete: 'Ich möchte _____ Kaffee, bitte.'
quiz.explanation: Kaffee is masculine ('der Kaffee'); in the accusative case it becomes 'einen Kaffee'.

units.title: Daily Routine
units.description: Describe your morning, work hours, meals, and evening habits.
units.grammarSummary: Separable verbs (trennbare Verben): prefixes split and go to the end of the clause (aufstehen -> Ich stehe um 7 Uhr auf).

lessons.title: Mein Tag
lessons.subtitle: Morning routines & separable verbs
lessons.grammarTip: In 'aufstehen', 'auf' splits and moves to the end of the sentence.

quiz.prompt: Where does the prefix 'auf' go in 'Ich stehe um 7 Uhr (aufstehen)'?
options: At the end of the sentence
quiz.explanation: Separable prefixes go to the very end of main clauses.

units.title: Shopping & Groceries
units.description: Buy clothes and groceries, ask prices, and understand receipts.
units.grammarSummary: Asking prices: 'Wie viel kostet...?' or 'Was kostet...?' Plural items take 'kosten'.

lessons.title: Im Supermarkt
lessons.subtitle: Prices, quantities and goods
lessons.grammarTip: Use 'Wie viel kostet der Apfel?' vs 'Wie viel kosten die Äpfel?'.

quiz.prompt: How do you ask 'How much does this cost?'
quiz.explanation: 'Wie viel kostet das?' is the standard price inquiry.

units.title: Directions & Places
units.description: Find places in town, ask for directions, and understand landmarks.
units.grammarSummary: Two-way prepositions take Dative for position ('Wo? Im Bahnhof') and Accusative for movement ('Wohin? In den Bahnhof').

lessons.title: Wo ist die Post?
lessons.subtitle: Navigating the city
lessons.grammarTip: Geradeaus (straight ahead), nach links (left), nach rechts (right).

words.exampleDe: Der Bahnhof ist in der Nähe.

quiz.prompt: What does 'geradeaus' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Geradeaus' means straight ahead.

units.title: Hobbies & Free Time
units.description: Talk about sports, music, weekend activities, and favorite pastimes.
units.grammarSummary: Expressing likes with 'gern': Place 'gern' after the conjugated verb (Ich spiele gern Fußball).

lessons.title: Was machst du gern?
lessons.subtitle: Expressing hobbies with 'gern'
lessons.grammarTip: 'Ich lese gern' = I like reading.

words.exampleDe: Ich lese am Abend ein Buch.
words.exampleEn: I read a book in the evening.
Do you like listening to music?

quiz.prompt: How do you say 'I like swimming'?
quiz.explanation: 'Ich schwimme gern' is the natural German expression.

levels.title: A2 • Elementary
levels.tagline: Build confidence: travel, past tense (Perfekt), healthcare, and housing.

units.title: Travel & Transport
units.description: Book train tickets, flights, and travel across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.
units.grammarSummary: Dative with 'mit': 'mit dem Zug' (masculine), 'mit dem Bus', 'mit der Bahn' (feminine).

lessons.title: Fahrkarten & Gleise
lessons.subtitle: Train announcements and schedules
lessons.grammarTip: 'Fahren mit' always requires the Dative case.

words.exampleDe: Der Zug fährt auf Gleis 3 ab.

quiz.prompt: Complete: 'Ich fahre mit _____ Zug.'
quiz.explanation: 'Mit' requires Dative; 'der Zug' becomes 'dem Zug'.

units.title: Doctor & Health
units.description: Describe symptoms, body parts, and understand doctor recommendations.
units.grammarSummary: Modal verb 'sollen' (should) for advice: 'Sie sollten viel Wasser trinken.'

lessons.title: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen
lessons.subtitle: Describing illness & pain
lessons.grammarTip: 'Wehtun' (to hurt): 'Mein Kopf tut weh' / 'Meine Augen tun weh.'

words.exampleDe: Ich habe einen Termin beim Arzt.
words.exampleEn: I have an appointment at the doctor.

quiz.prompt: How do you say 'My head hurts'?
quiz.explanation: 'Mein Kopf tut weh' is standard German for a headache.

units.title: Living & Home
units.description: Look for an apartment, describe rooms, and arrange furniture.
units.grammarSummary: Prepositions with Dative location: in, an, auf, unter, neben, zwischen.

lessons.title: Meine Wohnung
lessons.subtitle: Rooms and rent in German cities
lessons.grammarTip: 'Die Miete' is the monthly rent; 'Warmmiete' includes utilities.

quiz.prompt: What does 'Warmmiete' mean in rental listings?
quiz.explanation: 'Warmmiete' includes heating and ancillary building utility costs.

units.title: Past Events (Das Perfekt)
units.description: Master talking about what you did yesterday, last week, and in the past.
units.grammarSummary: Perfekt = haben/sein + Partizip II. Verbs of movement or change of state take 'sein'.

lessons.title: Was hast du gestern gemacht?
lessons.subtitle: Regular and irregular past participles
lessons.grammarTip: haben + gemacht / gearbeitet vs sein + gegangen / gefahren.

quiz.prompt: Which auxiliary verb pairs with 'nach Berlin gefahren'?
quiz.explanation: 'Fahren' indicates movement from A to B, so it requires 'sein' (er ist gefahren).

units.title: Weather & Seasons
units.description: Understand weather reports, talk about rain, snow, temperature, and seasons.
units.grammarSummary: Impersonal 'Es': 'Es regnet' (It rains), 'Es schneit' (It snows), 'Es ist kalt' (It is cold).

lessons.title: Wie ist das Wetter?
lessons.subtitle: Sun, snow, and degrees Celsius
lessons.grammarTip: Seasons are all masculine: der Frühling, der Sommer, der Herbst, der Winter.

quiz.prompt: What article do all German seasons take (Frühling, Sommer, Herbst, Winter)?
quiz.explanation: All four seasons are masculine: der Frühling, der Sommer, der Herbst, der Winter.

units.title: Work & Professions
units.description: Talk about occupations, working hours, colleagues, and office equipment.
units.grammarSummary: Feminine job titles add '-in': der Lehrer -> die Lehrerin, der Arzt -> die Ärztin.

lessons.title: Was bist du von Beruf?
lessons.subtitle: Jobs and daily tasks
lessons.grammarTip: In German you don't say 'Ich bin ein Lehrer', just 'Ich bin Lehrer'.

words.exampleEn: What do you do for a living?

quiz.prompt: How do you introduce your profession as an engineer in German?
quiz.explanation: German omits indefinite articles before professions ('Ich bin Ingenieur').

units.title: Clothing & Fashion
units.description: Sizes, colors, trying on clothes, and expressing style opinions.
units.grammarSummary: Adjective endings after indefinite articles: 'ein blauer Pullover', 'eine rote Jacke', 'ein grünes Hemd'.

lessons.title: Im Kleidergeschäft
lessons.subtitle: Trying on clothes & fits
lessons.grammarTip: 'Passen' (to fit size) vs 'stehen' (to suit/look good on someone).

quiz.prompt: Which verb means that clothes 'look good on someone'?
quiz.explanation: 'Das Kleid steht dir gut' means 'The dress suits you / looks good on you'.

units.title: Celebrations & Festivals
units.description: Birthdays, Christmas, invitations, congratulations, and giving gifts.
units.grammarSummary: Dative verbs: gratulieren (+ Dat), danken (+ Dat), schenken (+ Dat person, + Acc thing).

lessons.title: Herzlichen Glückwunsch!
lessons.subtitle: Wishes and birthday greetings
lessons.grammarTip: 'Ich gratuliere dir zum Geburtstag!' requires Dative pronoun 'dir'.

words.exampleEn: Thank you so much for the gift!

quiz.prompt: Complete: 'Ich gratuliere _____ zum Geburtstag!'
quiz.explanation: 'Gratulieren' governs the Dative case ('gratulieren + dir').

levels.title: B1 • Intermediate
levels.tagline: Conversational independence: complex clauses (weil, obwohl), career, and opinions.

units.title: Career & Job Applications
units.description: Write a CV, attend interviews, and present professional experience.
units.grammarSummary: Subordinate clauses with 'weil', 'dass', 'obwohl' move the conjugated verb to the very end.

lessons.title: Das Vorstellungsgespräch
lessons.subtitle: Interview strategies & qualifications
lessons.grammarTip: Conjugated verb goes last: '...weil ich Deutsch sprechen kann.'

words.exampleDe: Ich habe viel Erfahrung in Software.
words.exampleEn: I have lots of experience in software.

quiz.prompt: Where does the verb go after 'obwohl' (although)?
quiz.explanation: 'Obwohl' is a subordinating conjunction, sending the conjugated verb to the end.

units.title: Media & Technology
units.description: Discuss social media, news credibility, artificial intelligence, and privacy.
units.grammarSummary: Relative clauses: 'Das ist das Smartphone, das ich gekauft habe.'

lessons.title: Im digitalen Zeitalter
lessons.subtitle: Internet, apps, and privacy
lessons.grammarTip: Relative pronouns match gender of the noun and case of the subordinate clause.

words.exampleDe: Ich habe die Nachrichten im Radio gehört.
words.exampleEn: I heard the news on the radio.

quiz.prompt: What relative pronoun completes: 'Der Computer, _____ ich gestern kaufte, ist schnell.'?
quiz.explanation: 'Den' is masculine accusative for the direct object of 'kaufte'.

units.title: Environment & Nature
units.description: Discuss climate, recycling, renewable energy, and animal conservation.
units.grammarSummary: Passive voice in present tense: werden + Partizip II (z.B. 'Müll wird getrennt').

lessons.title: Klimaschutz im Alltag
lessons.subtitle: Recycling and renewable energy
lessons.grammarTip: Vorgangspassiv: 'werden' conjugates, Partizip II at end.

quiz.prompt: How is the passive voice formed in German present tense?
quiz.explanation: Present passive is formed with 'werden + Partizip II' (e.g. Das Haus wird gebaut).

units.title: Relationships & Feelings
units.description: Express emotional states, handle misunderstandings, and describe personality.
units.grammarSummary: Reflexive verbs with Accusative and Dative: 'sich freuen auf/über', 'sich ärgern über'.

lessons.title: Sich freuen & ärgern
lessons.subtitle: Prepositional reflexive verbs
lessons.grammarTip: 'Sich freuen auf' = looking forward to; 'sich freuen über' = happy about something present.

quiz.prompt: Which preposition means 'looking forward to' with 'sich freuen'?
quiz.explanation: 'Sich freuen auf (+ Acc)' means looking forward to a future event.

units.title: Education & Studies
units.description: Navigate German university life, vocational training (Duale Ausbildung), and exams.
units.grammarSummary: Infinitives with 'zu': 'Es ist wichtig, regelmäßig zu lernen.'

lessons.title: An der Universität
lessons.subtitle: Lectures, degrees, and dual training
lessons.grammarTip: With separable verbs, 'zu' sits between prefix and stem: 'aufzustehen'.

quiz.prompt: How is 'zu' placed with separable verb 'teilnehmen'?
quiz.explanation: In separable verbs, 'zu' inserts between prefix and root: 'teilzunehmen'.

units.title: Cultural Differences
units.description: Understand German customs, punctuality, trash separation etiquette, and small talk.
units.grammarSummary: Comparative and Superlative: schnell, schneller, am schnellsten; gut, besser, am besten.

lessons.title: Typisch deutsch?
lessons.subtitle: Punctuality, directness, and traditions
lessons.grammarTip: Use 'als' for comparisons: 'Er ist pünktlicher als ich.'

quiz.prompt: Which word follows comparatives in German (e.g. 'besser _____')?
quiz.explanation: Comparative unequal comparisons take 'als' (e.g. 'besser als').

units.title: Society & Politics
units.description: Understand elections, social structures, civic participation, and public news.
units.grammarSummary: Genitive case: 'des Tages', 'der Stadt', 'eines Gesetzes' to show possession.

lessons.title: Demokratie & Rechte
lessons.subtitle: Laws, elections, and civic rights
lessons.grammarTip: Masculine and neuter genitive nouns add -(e)s (des Staates).

words.exampleDe: Das Gesetz gilt für alle Bürger.
words.exampleEn: The law applies to all citizens.
Freedom of speech is a fundamental right.

quiz.prompt: What is the Genitive form of 'der Bürger' (the citizen)?
quiz.explanation: Masculine Genitive is 'des Bürgers'.

units.title: Dreams & Future Plans
units.description: Express hopes, future predictions, and wishes with Futur I and Konjunktiv II basics.
units.grammarSummary: Futur I: werden + Infinitiv ('Ich werde nächstes Jahr nach Wien ziehen').

lessons.title: Meine Zukunft
lessons.subtitle: Plans, goals, and Futur I
lessons.grammarTip: Futur I: 'Ich werde reisen', 'Du wirst lernen'.

quiz.prompt: Complete with Futur I: 'Ich _____ im Sommer eine Reise machen.'
quiz.explanation: 'Werde' is 1st person singular of 'werden' for future tense.

levels.title: B2 • Upper Intermediate
levels.tagline: Nuanced fluency: professional diplomacy, Konjunktiv II, idioms, and high-level debate.

units.title: Business Communication
units.description: Professional negotiations, formal email correspondence, and business meetings.
units.grammarSummary: Nominalization (Nominalisierung): converting verbs and adjectives into concise corporate nouns.

lessons.title: Verhandlungen führen
lessons.subtitle: Negotiations & business diplomacy
lessons.grammarTip: Use indirect polite formulations with Konjunktiv II ('Könnten Sie bitte...').

words.exampleDe: Aus unserer Sicht ist dieser Standpunkt begründet.
words.exampleEn: From our perspective, this stance is justified.

quiz.prompt: Which ending produces a 100% feminine business noun?
quiz.explanation: Nouns ending in '-ung' are always feminine (die Verhandlung, die Vereinbarung).

units.title: Science & Innovation
units.description: Analyze scientific papers, discuss medical breakthroughs, and explore tech disruption.
units.grammarSummary: Participle constructions as adjectives: 'die steigenden Preise' / 'die gelösten Probleme'.

lessons.title: Künstliche Intelligenz
lessons.subtitle: Technological disruption & research
lessons.grammarTip: Partizip I (+d) indicates an active ongoing action: 'die forschende Gruppe'.

quiz.prompt: What does Partizip I 'die schlafenden Kinder' express?
quiz.explanation: Partizip I ('schlafend') functions as an active present participle ('the sleeping children').

units.title: Debates & Discussions
units.description: Weigh pros and cons, challenge arguments constructively, and lead discussions.
units.grammarSummary: Two-part connectors: 'sowohl ... als auch', 'weder ... noch', 'einerseits ... andererseits'.

lessons.title: Pro und Kontra
lessons.subtitle: Balancing nuanced perspectives
lessons.grammarTip: 'Einerseits' / 'andererseits' show opposing sides of an argument.

words.exampleDe: In diesem Zusammenhang ist das relevant.
words.exampleEn: In this context, that is relevant.
I must disagree with you there.

quiz.prompt: Which connector pairs with 'weder' to mean 'neither... nor'?
quiz.explanation: 'Weder ... noch' means 'neither ... nor'.

units.title: Art, Music & Literature
units.description: Interpret German literature, cinema, theater productions, and classical music.
units.grammarSummary: Zustandspassiv (sein + Partizip II) vs Vorgangspassiv (werden + Partizip II).

lessons.title: Kulturkritik
lessons.subtitle: Reviews, theater, and fine art
lessons.grammarTip: 'Das Museum ist geöffnet' (state) vs 'Das Museum wird geöffnet' (action).

quiz.prompt: Which sentence expresses Zustandspassiv (state of being)?
quiz.explanation: 'Ist geschlossen' describes the resulting state (Zustandspassiv).

units.title: Psychology & Behavior
units.description: Explore motivation, stress management, subconscious habits, and human psychology.
units.grammarSummary: Subjunctive I (Konjunktiv I) used for reported speech in formal news.

lessons.title: Verhaltensmuster
lessons.subtitle: Habits, stress, and motivation
lessons.grammarTip: Konjunktiv I is based on the infinitive root: 'er habe', 'er sei'.

quiz.prompt: Where is Konjunktiv I predominantly used in Germany?
quiz.explanation: Konjunktiv I is primarily used in formal journalism and reported speech.

units.title: Law & Global Ethics
units.description: Analyze international treaties, fundamental rights, and contemporary ethical dilemmas.
units.grammarSummary: Modal-like passive substitutes: 'sein + zu + Infinitiv' ('Das Problem ist zu lösen' = can/must be solved).

lessons.title: Ethische Grundsätze
lessons.subtitle: Legal frameworks and ethical dilemmas
lessons.grammarTip: 'Das ist nicht zu tolerieren' = That cannot be tolerated.

words.exampleDe: Gerechtigkeit ist ein Grundpfeiler des Staates.
words.exampleEn: Justice is a cornerstone of the state.

words.exampleDe: Wir tragen Verantwortung für zukünftige Generationen.
words.exampleEn: We bear responsibility for future generations.

quiz.prompt: What does 'Diese Aufgabe ist bis morgen zu erledigen' mean?
options: This task must be done by tomorrow
quiz.explanation: 'Sein + zu + Infinitiv' expresses obligation ('must be done').

units.title: Idioms & Expressions
units.description: Master colorful German idioms, metaphorical proverbs, and colloquial expressions.
units.grammarSummary: Fixed prepositional verbs and idiomatic metaphors in everyday colloquial speech.

lessons.title: Typische Redewendungen
lessons.subtitle: Common idioms and sayings
lessons.grammarTip: 'Daumen drücken' (wish luck), 'ins Fettnäpfchen treten' (put foot in mouth).

words.english: to wish luck / keep fingers crossed
words.exampleDe: Ich drücke dir fest die Daumen!
words.exampleEn: I'll keep my fingers crossed for you!

words.german: Zwei Fliegen mit einer Klappe schlagen
words.english: kill two birds with one stone
words.exampleDe: Damit schlagen wir zwei Fliegen mit einer Klappe.
words.exampleEn: With that we kill two birds with one stone.

quiz.prompt: What does 'Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof' mean?
options: I want to buy a ticket
quiz.explanation: 'Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof' is a classic idiom meaning 'It's all Greek to me / I understand nothing'.

units.title: Advanced Grammar Mastery
units.description: Synthesize all advanced B2 structures: Konjunktiv II, Passiv, and complex hypotheticals.
units.grammarSummary: Konjunktiv II past tense: 'wäre gewesen', 'hätte gehabt', 'hätte machen können'.

lessons.title: Irreale Bedingungen
lessons.subtitle: Unreal past conditions with Konjunktiv II
lessons.grammarTip: 'Wenn ich das gewusst hätte, wäre ich gekommen.'

quiz.prompt: Complete: 'Wenn ich Zeit gehabt hätte, _____ ich mitgekommen.'
quiz.explanation: 'Mitkommen' uses 'sein' in perfect tenses, so in past Konjunktiv II it is 'wäre mitgekommen'.
